cities.funFact: Tokyo is the world's most populated metropolitan area, home to over 37 million people — that's more than the entire country of Canada!

clues.text: Jaime watched chefs at a world-famous fish market auction off an enormous tuna in the early hours of the morning.
Thousands of people gathered under trees bursting with pink blossoms, picnicking and celebrating the arrival of spring.
Jeff zoomed through the countryside on a bullet train so fast that a famous snow-capped mountain was just a white blur out the window!

cities.funFact: London's underground railway — called the Tube — is the oldest metro system in the world, opening all the way back in 1863!

clues.text: Jaime spotted bright red double-decker buses weaving through busy streets lined with enormous museums on every corner.
Jeff photographed a giant clock tower that chimes every quarter hour — its deep bells can be heard all across the city.
A guard in a tall furry black hat stood perfectly still outside a royal palace — he was not allowed to smile, no matter what!

cities.funFact: Buenos Aires is called the 'Paris of South America' because of its wide tree-lined boulevards and European-style architecture!

clues.text: They spotted couples dancing cheek to cheek in a dramatic style, dipping and spinning to passionate music right in the street.
Jeff wrote home: 'We had the most amazing grilled beef at a cookout called an asado — everyone here loves it!'
A fan showed Jaime a jersey from a football legend — many call him the greatest of all time, and he was born right here in this city.

cities.funFact: Sydney is home to the famous Opera House — one of the most recognisable buildings in the world, with its iconic sail-like roof sitting right on Sydney Harbour!

clues.text: Jaime saw a building shaped like giant white shells sitting on the edge of a sparkling harbour — one of the most photographed buildings on Earth.
Jeff spotted an animal hopping along a dusty trail — this creature lives naturally in only one country in the whole world.
A surf instructor told them people here have been riding ocean waves since before it was recognised as a sport anywhere else.

cities.funFact: Lima is one of the largest cities in South America and sits right on the Pacific coast — you can watch the sun set over the ocean every evening!

clues.text: Jeff stood on a high cliff and watched paragliders soaring out over the Pacific Ocean — the city stretches right to the edge of the coast.
Jaime tasted ceviche — fresh raw fish marinated in citrus juice and chilli — a dish said to have been invented right here in this city.
They explored a grand historic main square surrounded by a cathedral and colonial palaces built hundreds of years ago.

cities.funFact: Rome is called the 'Eternal City' and has been continuously inhabited for over 2,800 years — making it one of the oldest cities in the world!

clues.text: They bought tickets to visit a huge oval stone arena where thousands once watched gladiators battle — still standing after nearly 2,000 years!
Jeff found the original pizza — just flatbread with tomato and melted cheese, no extra toppings, eaten folded in half in the street.
Jaime threw a coin into an enormous ornate fountain to make a wish — over a million coins are tossed in by visitors every single year.

cities.funFact: Seoul is one of the most connected cities in the world — South Korea has the fastest average internet speeds on the planet!

clues.text: Jeff bought a colourful Talchum mask at a street market — used in traditional performances he watched in the old palace grounds.
Jaime spent an hour listening to K-Pop in a music shop and asked the owner for a poster of her favourite group.
A tech journalist spotted them at an electronics fair in a city famous for being home to one of the world's biggest phone companies.

cities.funFact: Madrid is the highest capital city in the European Union, sitting 667 metres above sea level — and it's home to the Prado Museum, one of the world's greatest art galleries!

clues.text: Jeff watched performers on a street corner stomping their feet and clicking castanets in a fiery, passionate dance.
Jaime read a poster about a famous festival where brave runners dash through narrow streets with bulls charging right behind them.
A chef served them paella — a colourful dish of rice, seafood, and vegetables all cooked together in one giant flat pan.

cities.funFact: Paris has more than 1,800 patisseries (pastry shops) and is considered the world capital of fashion and fine art!

clues.text: Jaime looked up at a giant iron tower twinkling with thousands of lights — after dark it sparkles every hour for five whole minutes!
Jeff stopped at a bakery and tried a buttery, flaky crescent-shaped pastry that people here eat for breakfast every single morning.
They spent an afternoon in the world's most visited art museum, gazing at a famous portrait of a woman with a mysterious smile.

cities.funFact: Nairobi is the only capital city in the world with a national park right inside its boundaries — you can watch lions and giraffes roam with city skyscrapers in the background!

clues.text: Jeff saw a lion resting in the shade while zebras grazed nearby — with the glittering city skyline visible right behind them.
Jaime spoke to a safari guide who said this city is the only capital in the world with a national park right inside its boundaries.
A coach told them this country produces some of the world's greatest long-distance runners — with more Olympic gold medals than almost anywhere else.

cities.funFact: Cape Town sits at the foot of Table Mountain — a famous flat-topped mountain that often has a 'tablecloth' of cloud rolling over it!

clues.text: Jeff spotted a whole colony of penguins waddling along a beach — the only place in Africa where they live in the wild.
Jaime looked up and saw a famous flat-topped mountain standing right over the city, like a giant natural table in the sky.
A local told them their country is called the 'Rainbow Nation' because so many different cultures, languages, and peoples live side by side here.

cities.funFact: Mexico City was built on the ruins of the ancient Aztec capital Tenochtitlan — and incredible pyramids are just a short drive away!

clues.text: Jeff tried a soft corn tortilla filled with spiced meat and fresh herbs — sold from a street stall on practically every single corner.
Jaime heard a mariachi band playing guitars, trumpets, and violins in the main square — everyone nearby clapping and singing along.
They visited ancient stone pyramids just outside the city — built over a thousand years ago by one of the world's most powerful civilisations.
